newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says helping Moslem Africa top priority.
newsitem.headline: Iran says helping Moslem Africa top priority.

text.p: Iran is giving top priority to helping African states, particularly Moslem countries, which it sees as an Islamic duty, Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said on Friday.

"The Islamic Republic of Iran will in the future have an earnest and notable presence in Africa as its top priority and in under-developed Asian states as a second priority," Rafsanjani said in a prayer sermon broadcast on Tehran radio.

"This is a religious tax that our revolution will have to pay to thank God...However this is a tax that will not have costs for us and could result in income too, but unlike arrogance (West) and colonialism, our goal is not to profit," Rafsanjani, a Shi'ite cleric, added.
He said the cabinet had recently drawn up a plan to boost ties particularly with Moslem countries in Africa to help them in sectors including education, industry and agriculture.

The remarks came as Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati is on a tour of some 12 African countries to invite their leaders to attend an Islamic summit in Tehran in December. He has already visited Tunisia, Gambia and Guinea.
"We could be giving financial aid...or give credits to pay for services we would be providing or we could use some of their resources as payment for their projects," Rafsanjani said.
Iran has been trying to raise its profile in Africa and Rafsanjani last year mediated in a dispute between Uganda and Islamic Sudan during a rare tour of the continent.
The drive is part of efforts by Tehran to fight Washington's attempts to isolate the Islamic republic. Iran also sees Africa as a potential market for its goods and services.
Iran and Mozambique on Thursday signed a memorandum of understanding on building an oil refinery in the African state.
